The mod-two boundary ranks independently agree. No infinite statement follows from this finite proof.

originality.rationale: The novelty-bearing conclusion is an explicit 105-pair relative elementary collapse of the two-independence complex onto the ordinary independence complex of the canonical eleven-vertex Grötzsch graph. Earlier ordinary Mycielski suspension formulas can explain the ordinary homotopy type but do not imply that this inclusion is a simple-homotopy equivalence. The most relevant higher-independence sources treat trees, complete multipartite and other specified families, or a different generalized Mycielskian. Published mathematical-record retrieval for aliases and inclusion/deformation terminology yielded no equivalent or stronger result. Residual bibliographic uncertainty is acknowledged.

value.rationale: The Grötzsch graph is a canonical smallest triangle-free four-chromatic graph and a basic Mycielski test case. The higher-independence filtration often changes homotopy and can introduce torsion even on related generalized Mycielskians, so the exact fact that its first nontrivial enlargement has a relative simplicial collapse is a motivated inclusion-level structural result, stronger than an isolated Betti number. The 105 explicit collapses provide a reusable benchmark for investigating which graph operations preserve simple-homotopy type.
